**Nine stops, in the order you meet them.** The last column is there to be ticked: printed, or in
the Word copy, this table is the checklist for one piece of analysis.

| Where you are | Where to read it | What you do there | What you leave behind | Done |
|----------------|----------------|-----------------------------------|----------------------------|-----|
| You have been asked to do a piece of analysis | [How to use this playbook](/guidance/00-how-to-use/index.qmd) | Take the short path: decide your assurance level, then find what it requires. Five minutes and one page. Everything else exists for when you need it | Nothing recorded yet. What you have is the two things you need to start | ☐ |
| Is this the question they meant to ask? | [Phase 1. Engagement and scoping](/guidance/01-engagement-and-scoping/index.qmd) | Agree the decision the analysis supports, the question, what is out of scope, and the deadline. Where a request arrives framed as an output, you are expected to reframe it as a question | The scope and specification, with the question in one sentence and the record of the conversation that got you there | ☐ |
| How much assurance does this need? | [Deciding your assurance level](/guidance/07-deciding-your-assurance-level/index.qmd) | Score six impact dimensions and six likelihood dimensions with your commissioner, take the highest of each, and read the level off the matrix. About five minutes, at scoping and not later | The completed assurance level decision sheet, attached to the specification, with the Business Critical answer recorded either way | ☐ |
| What do I actually have to do? | [The checks, by level](/guidance/07-deciding-your-assurance-level/index.qmd#the-checks-by-level) | Read the block for your level and the blocks inside it. The checks are cumulative: your level does everything the levels below it do and adds its own. Name your reviewer before you start | The quality assurance checklist for your level, and a named reviewer with time in the schedule | ☐ |
| What do I not know, and how much does it matter? | [Uncertainty, assumptions and limitations](/guidance/09-resources/r10-uncertainty.qmd) | Find the principal sources of uncertainty while there is still time to design for them. Agree with your commissioner how certain the answer needs to be | Assumptions listed with their rationale and the effect if wrong, and the uncertainty section of the project record | ☐ |
| Someone independent needs to check this | [Phase 3. Analysis](/guidance/03-analysis/index.qmd) | Do your own verification and validation first, then hand it to the critical friend named at design. Their findings are yours to act on. Your own checks are the first line, not the last one | The quality assurance log: what was checked, when, and what was found | ☐ |
| How do I write this up without overclaiming? | [Phase 4. Delivery and sign-off](/guidance/04-delivery-and-sign-off/index.qmd) | State the caveats in the output itself, not only in an annex, and produce the quality assurance statement your level requires. Say what the results can and cannot be used for | The output and the quality assurance statement, published with it at Level 3 | ☐ |
| Is any of this ethically or legally loaded? | [Ethics and transparency](/guidance/09-resources/r11-ethics-and-personal-data.qmd) | Check the position on the Data and AI Ethics Framework, on personal data, and on whether any algorithmic tool is in Algorithmic Transparency Recording Standard scope. Ask information governance before the work starts | The ethics position recorded, and a transparency record drafted where the tool is in scope | ☐ |
| It is out. Now what? | [Phase 5. Review](/guidance/05-review/index.qmd) | Ask whether the analysis informed the decision, whether it is still used, whether it is still right, and whether it should be decommissioned. At Level 1 the review is yours to own | The review record, and the lessons recorded where the next analyst will look for them | ☐ |

**One branch, after the assurance level stop.** Any single impact dimension scored 4 makes the work
Business Critical. That brings Level 4 BCA, a register entry and a named Analysis Senior Responsible
Officer, all starting at scoping. [Business Critical analysis](/guidance/08-business-critical/index.qmd) is the route
in nine steps, and everything else on this list still applies.
